name: abs
description: The `abs()` function returns the non‑negative magnitude of its argument, whether it’s an integer, float, complex number, or any object that defines an `__abs__` method.

name: aiter
description: The `aiter()` function returns an asynchronous iterator from a given asynchronous iterable by invoking its `__aiter__` method.

name: all
description: The `all()` function returns True when every element in a given iterable evaluates to true (or when the iterable is empty), otherwise it returns False.

name: anext
description: `anext()` asynchronously retrieves the next element from an async iterator, optionally returning a provided default instead of raising StopAsyncIteration when the iterator is exhausted.

name: any
description: The `any()` function iterates through an iterable and returns True as soon as it finds a truthy element, otherwise it returns False if no such element exists or the iterable is empty.

name: ascii
description: The ascii() function returns a printable string representation of an object like repr(), but with any non‑ASCII characters escaped using \x, \u, or \U sequences.

name: bin
description: The bin() function takes an integer (or any object implementing __index__) and returns its binary representation as a string prefixed with “0b”.

name: bool
description: The bool() function converts a given argument (or defaults to False if omitted) to its Boolean truth value, returning True for any truthy input and False otherwise.

name: breakpoint
description: The `breakpoint()` function conveniently invokes the current debugger (by default `pdb.set_trace()`) at the call site, allowing customization via `sys.breakpointhook()` or the `PYTHONBREAKPOINT` environment variable.

name: bytearray
description: `bytearray()` creates a mutable sequence of bytes that can be initialized from a string (with encoding), an integer size, a buffer, an iterable of integers 0–255, or left empty.

name: bytes
description: The `bytes()` function creates an immutable sequence of integer values (0–255) from the given input, providing a read‑only version of a bytearray with the same indexing, slicing, and non‑mutating methods.

name: callable
description: callable() returns True when the given object can be invoked like a function (including classes and objects with a __call__ method) and False otherwise.

name: chr
description: chr() converts an integer Unicode code point (0–0x10FFFF) into the corresponding one‑character string, raising ValueError for out‑of‑range values.

name: classmethod
description: classmethod() converts a regular function into a method that receives the owning class as its first argument, allowing it to be invoked on both the class itself and its instances.

name: compile
description: The `compile()` function transforms source code (as a string, bytes, or AST) into a code object—according to the specified mode, filename, flags, and optimization level—so it can be executed by `exec()` or `eval()`.

name: complex
description: The `complex()` function converts a string or numeric input (or separate real and imaginary parts) into a Python complex number, handling various formats and falling back to an object’s `__complex__`, `__float__`, or `__index__` methods when needed.

name: delattr
description: delattr() removes a specified attribute from an object by name, performing the same operation as the del statement on that attribute.

name: dict
description: The dict() function constructs a new dictionary object, optionally initializing it from a mapping, iterable of key‑value pairs, or keyword arguments.

name: dir
description: The dir() function returns a sorted list of attribute names for the given object (or for the current local scope if called without arguments), using __dir__ if defined, otherwise gathering from the object’s __dict__, type, and related classes.

name: divmod
description: The divmod() function takes two numbers and returns a two‑element tuple containing the integer quotient and the remainder of their division, following the same rules as floor division and modulo for the given operand types.

name: enumerate
description: enumerate() returns an iterator that yields pairs of a running index (starting from a specified value, default 0) and each element from the given iterable.

name: eval
description: It evaluates a given Python expression (or compiled code object) at runtime and returns its result, optionally using specified global and local namespaces.

name: exec
description: exec() dynamically runs a string or code object as Python statements within optional global and local namespaces, returning None.

name: filter
description: The `filter()` function creates an iterator that yields each element from a given iterable for which a specified predicate function returns True (or, if the function is None, yields only the truthy elements).

name: float
description: The float() function converts a numeric value or a properly formatted numeric string—including optional sign, whitespace, exponent, infinity, or NaN—into a Python floating‑point number, or returns 0.0 when called without arguments.

name: format
description: The `format()` function converts a given value into a string representation according to a format specification (or defaults to `str(value)` if none is provided) by invoking the value’s `__format__` method and raising a TypeError for invalid specifications.

name: frozenset
description: frozenset() creates an immutable set object that can be initialized from an iterable, allowing membership testing and set operations without permitting modification of its elements.

name: getattr
description: getattr() returns the value of a specified attribute of an object, optionally providing a default value instead of raising an AttributeError if the attribute does not exist.

name: globals
description: globals() returns a dictionary representing the current module’s global symbol table, reflecting the namespace in which the function was defined regardless of where it is later called.

name: hasattr
description: The `hasattr()` function checks whether a given object possesses an attribute with a specified name, returning True if it exists and False otherwise.

name: hash
description: The `hash()` function returns an integer hash value for an object (if it has one) that is used for fast dictionary key comparison, ensuring objects that compare equal share the same hash, with the result truncated to the host machine’s pointer size.

name: help
description: The built‑in `help()` function launches Python’s interactive help system, displaying documentation for a given name, object, or, when called without arguments, starting the full help interface on the console.

name: hex
description: The hex() function returns a string representing a given integer in lowercase hexadecimal form prefixed with “0x”, handling negative numbers and objects that implement __index__().

name: id
description: The `id()` function returns a unique, constant integer that identifies a specific object for the duration of its existence, typically reflecting the object's memory address in CPython.

name: input
description: The built‑in input() function optionally displays a prompt, reads a line from standard input, strips the trailing newline, returns the resulting string, and raises EOFError on end‑of‑file.

name: int
description: The int() function creates an integer object by converting a number, a string (optionally with a specified base), or an object implementing __int__ or __index__, returning 0 when called without arguments.

name: isinstance
description: `isinstance()` returns True when a given object is an instance of a specified class, subclass, or any type listed in a tuple/union, and False otherwise, raising a TypeError only if the classinfo argument is not a valid type specification.

name: issubclass
description: issubclass() checks whether a given class (or its subclasses) is a subclass of specified class(es) or a Union type, returning True if it is (including when the class equals itself) and raising TypeError for invalid arguments.

name: iter
description: The `iter()` function creates an iterator either from an iterable or sequence when called with one argument, or from a callable that repeatedly produces values until a specified sentinel value signals termination when called with two arguments.

name: len
description: len() returns the number of items in a sequence or collection, raising OverflowError if the count exceeds sys.maxsize.

name: list
description: The list() function creates a new mutable sequence object (a list) from an iterable, allowing you to initialize or convert data into a list.

name: locals
description: `locals()` returns a mutable mapping of the current scope’s variable names to their bound objects, reflecting and updating the local symbol table (or providing a snapshot in optimized function scopes).

name: map
description: The `map()` function returns an iterator that lazily applies a given function to each element of one or more iterables in parallel, producing the function’s results until the shortest iterable is exhausted (or raising a ValueError if `strict=True` and lengths differ).

name: max
description: The max() function returns the greatest element from a single iterable or the greatest of multiple given arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value to return when the iterable is empty.

name: memoryview
description: `memoryview()` creates a lightweight object that provides read‑only or writable access to the underlying byte-oriented buffer of another object without copying its data.

name: min
description: The min() function returns the smallest element from a single iterable or the smallest of multiple given arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value for empty iterables.

name: next
description: The `next()` function returns the subsequent element of an iterator by invoking its `__next__()` method, optionally providing a default value to return instead of raising `StopIteration` when the iterator is exhausted.

name: object
description: The `object()` function creates a minimal, feature‑less instance of Python’s ultimate base class, which has no arguments, no `__dict__`, and provides only the fundamental methods shared by all objects.

name: oct
description: The oct() function returns a string representation of an integer in octal notation, prefixed with “0o”, and works with any object that defines an __index__() method.

name: open
description: The open() function opens a file (or file descriptor) with a specified mode and optional parameters and returns a corresponding file object for reading, writing, or appending, raising an OSError if the operation fails.

name: ord
description: The `ord()` function returns the integer Unicode code point of a single-character string or the numeric byte value of a one‑byte bytes/bytearray object.

name: pow
description: The pow() function computes base raised to the exponent, optionally performing modular exponentiation when a third argument is provided, handling mixed numeric types and returning floats, integers, or complex numbers as appropriate.

name: print
description: The `print()` function writes the string representations of given objects to a text stream (defaulting to standard output), separating them with a specified delimiter, ending with a specified string, and optionally flushing the stream.

name: property
description: The `property()` function creates a descriptor that links optional getter, setter, and deleter callables to an attribute name, allowing attribute access, assignment, and deletion to invoke those functions while optionally providing a docstring.

name: getter
description: The `getter()` function retrieves and returns a specific value or object from a data source or structure based on the provided parameters.

name: setter
description: The setter() function assigns a new value to a specified attribute, optionally performing validation or additional processing before updating the object's state.

name: deleter
description: The `deleter()` method creates a new property object identical to the original but with its `fdel` accessor replaced by the decorated function, enabling deletion of the underlying attribute.

name: __name__
description: `__name__` is a special attribute that holds the identifier of a module, class, function, or variable, allowing its name to be accessed (and, for certain objects, modified) at runtime.

name: range
description: The `range()` function creates an immutable sequence of numbers defined by a start, stop, and optional step, allowing efficient iteration without storing all values in memory.

name: repr
description: The `repr()` function returns a string that provides an official, unambiguous representation of an object, typically one that could be used with `eval()` to recreate the object, and falls back to a descriptive placeholder if such a representation isn’t possible.

name: reversed
description: The `reversed()` function returns an iterator that yields the elements of a sequence or any object with a __reversed__ method in the opposite order from which they appear.

name: round
description: The round() function returns a number rounded to the specified number of decimal places (or to the nearest integer if no ndigits is given), using “bankers rounding” where ties are rounded to the nearest even value.

name: set
description: The `set()` function creates and returns a new mutable set object, optionally populating it with unique elements drawn from a given iterable.

name: setattr
description: setattr(obj, name, value) assigns the given value to the attribute named by the string on the specified object, effectively performing the same operation as obj.name = value.

name: slice
description: The slice() function creates a slice object that defines a range of indices (with optional start, stop, and step values) for use in slicing operations such as a[start:stop:step].

name: start
description: The start() function merely assigns its input arguments (or their defaults) to read‑only attributes, providing values that NumPy and other third‑party packages can later access.

name: sorted
description: The sorted() function returns a new list containing the elements of a given iterable arranged in order, optionally using a key function to extract comparison values and a reverse flag to invert the sorting direction, while preserving the original order of equal elements.

name: staticmethod
description: It converts a function defined in a class into a static method that can be called on the class or its instances without receiving an automatic first argument.

name: str
description: The `str()` function converts any given object to its string representation, returning a new string that reflects the object’s value.

name: sum
description: The `sum()` function iteratively adds the elements of an iterable to an optional start value, returning their total.

name: super
description: super() returns a proxy that automatically resolves method and attribute lookups to the next class in the method resolution order, enabling calls to overridden or cooperative superclass implementations without hard‑coding class names.

name: tuple
description: The `tuple()` function creates an immutable ordered sequence by converting an iterable (or returning an empty tuple when called without arguments).

name: type
description: The `type()` function returns an object's type when called with one argument and dynamically creates a new class when called with three arguments (name, bases, and dict).

name: vars
description: The vars() function returns an object’s __dict__ attribute (or the current locals dictionary when called without arguments), allowing inspection of its mutable attribute mapping but raising TypeError if the object lacks a __dict__.

name: zip
description: zip() lazily combines multiple iterables element‑wise into tuples, stopping at the shortest iterable unless strict=True is used to require equal lengths.

name: __import__
description: `__import__()` is a low‑level built‑in function that performs the actual module loading used by the import statement, allowing optional control of globals, locals, from‑list objects, and relative‑import level, but is generally discouraged in favor of `importlib.import_module()`.
